Living in a hamlet in rural India that gets plenty of snow, this happens way too often. The longest has been 8 days in deep winter. I have two UPS', one for the modem and router, another for the satellite dish and TV. There are torches and candles all around, the bathroom has a simple LED battery light as well. What we do is defined by how long the power is gone for:

1 hr: Continue as usual, the UPS can take the load, check with the local power office at the end of the hour to get an idea whats happening

2 hr: Switch off the UPS, esp. if the power is gonna be gone for long

4 hr: Use 3G/2G on the phone to browse/email, use LED lights for illumination

8 hr: Take out the always charged battery packs to recharge phones

1 day: Take out the backup Nokia, switch SIM cards, and use it sparingly, start eating all the meats, gift what can't be eaten, if its winter light up the only fireplace in the living room, and everyone sleeps there. Catch up on your reading on the eBook reader.

2 days: Clean up the fridge, throw the rotting food, if its deep winter and snow, make a freezer in the snow. Collect more wood! Continue reading on the eBook readers. Walk a few kms in 3 ft of snow and buy more candles.

4 days: Switch to regular books, heat up water on the fireplace for baths, collect even more wood, since fresh vegetables are now gone, start eating canned beans, canned tuna, lentils and rice.

8 days: Nokia is still going strong, usage is now limited to 4 calls a day, its been a week since one used the net or saw TV. Tiredness takes over, no more reading, plans are made to move where there is no snow.

The entirety of the internet is the frontier, if you think about it. We have curated, monetized communities like Reddit and things like IRC. Sure, moderation is more common than not these days but you're not forced to be on Reddit or Voat.

"The Internet is the first thing that humanity has built that humanity doesn't understand, the largest experiment in anarchy that we have ever had." - Eric Schmidt

That's very true, and if you look at the last many years you discover that humanity will form governance around itself. The internet has become a moderated place, but only because people wanted it to be moderated. We can throw around cries of free speech, and that's good, but at the same time you need to be mindful of coming off like a twat. We're all in the wild-west, and only now is it starting to become industrialized. Only now are Congressmen talking about the internet, which they don't really get, companies are learning they can use this amazing tool to make money on a scale thought impossible.

We literally walk around with a connection to the entirety of human knowledge and resource. You can download a copy of Wikipedia right now, you can look up chemical properties, learn another language (or a coding language.), you can talk to someone in China like they're next to you. Let's not think that we don't live in an incredible age, because that would be vastly underestimating the awesomeness of our world.

EFF, or Electronic Frontier Foundation, recognized the importance of "internet freedoms" 25 years ago. No I'm not a spokesman for them or anything like that...just sayin' if you haven't checked em out or heard of them please take a look. They've been fighting for us this whole time.

PS: This isn't necessarily directed at OP I'm just being an EFF whore.
